prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1064; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured driver. Vehicles came to rest in the travel lane with minor front-end damage reported on both units. Police report requested and pending. Claimant reports wrist pain and has been advised to seek medical evaluation.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. Claimant describes slowing for traffic when the other vehicle crossed the centerline. Claimant reports a fractured wrist confirmed by urgent care imaging and is currently in a splint. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been given the claims contact line and the process for submitting medical bills.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received and reviewed. Airbag deployment noted on the claimant's vehicle. Repair estimate ordered from an approved shop. Tow and rental coverage confirmed under the policy. Claimant asked about the timeline for a settlement decision; explained that the medical records and treatment status are needed before evaluation.

Entry 4: Requested the orthopedic records and the itemized medical bills from the claimant's provider, with signed authorization obtained. Follow-up call placed to the claimant to confirm current symptoms and the treatment plan, including any follow-up appointments and whether a surgical consult has been recommended.

Entry 5: Police report received and reviewed. It supports the claimant's account of the centerline crossing by the other driver. Liability assessment in progress pending final repair estimate and medical documentation. Claimant reminded that they may still consult an attorney at any time and that no settlement offer has been made yet.
